headline_marked: July 24: [[Atif Aslam to perform in Dhaka]] after year-long wait
headline: July 24: Atif Aslam to perform in Dhaka after year-long wait
summary: The Pakistani singer's concert, postponed last December due to security concerns, is finally returning to Bangladesh.
details: Popular Pakistani singer Atif Aslam is returning to Bangladesh for a concert on July 24. The event, titled 'Main Stage Show featuring Atif Aslam', is being organized by Main Stage Incorporated.
The concert was originally scheduled for December 13 last year but was postponed just two days before the event due to security concerns following the announcement of the national election schedule.

Following the postponement, the organizers and Atif Aslam himself promised fans that the show would be rescheduled. Atif Aslam stated on his official Facebook page that previous ticket holders' tickets would remain valid.
Main Stage Incorporated has now secured all necessary cultural clearances, security permits, and official approvals to move forward with the event.

Fans who purchased tickets for the 2025 show but did not request refunds are not required to buy new tickets. They must complete a 'Re-Apply' process on the mainstage.show website to receive new tickets.
Those who previously requested refunds can also apply to withdraw their refund request and reinstate their tickets through the same website.
A limited number of new tickets will be sold via GetMyTicket.live, with pricing and category details to be released soon. The venue will also be announced in the following days.
Director Kazi Rafsan of Main Stage Incorporated stated that the team has spent the last few months coordinating with authorities to fulfill their promise to the fans.
caption:
Atif Aslam is finally returning to Dhaka! 🎤

After a year of waiting, the postponed concert is back on for July 24.

Popular Pakistani singer Atif Aslam is returning to Bangladesh for a concert on July 24. The event, titled 'Main Stage Show featuring Atif Aslam', is being organized by Main Stage Incorporated.

The concert was originally scheduled for December 13 last year but was postponed just two days before the event due to security concerns following the announcement of the national election schedule.

Following the postponement, the organizers and Atif Aslam himself promised fans that the show would be rescheduled. Atif Aslam stated on his official Facebook page that previous ticket holders' tickets would remain valid.

Main Stage Incorporated has now secured all necessary cultural clearances, security permits, and official approvals to move forward with the event.

Fans who purchased tickets for the 2025 show but did not request refunds are not required to buy new tickets. They must complete a 'Re-Apply' process on the mainstage.show website to receive new tickets.

Those who previously requested refunds can also apply to withdraw their refund request and reinstate their tickets through the same website.

A limited number of new tickets will be sold via GetMyTicket.live, with pricing and category details to be released soon. The venue will also be announced in the following days.

Director Kazi Rafsan of Main Stage Incorporated stated that the team has spent the last few months coordinating with authorities to fulfill their promise to the fans.

headline_marked: At least [[32 dead, 700 injured]] in twin earthquakes rock Venezuela
headline: At least 32 dead, 700 injured in twin earthquakes rock Venezuela
summary: A state of emergency has been declared as devastating quakes topple buildings in Caracas and leave many trapped in rubble.
details: Two strong earthquakes struck west of Venezuela's capital, Caracas, on Wednesday afternoon, causing widespread destruction and toppling buildings across the country.
The interim president reported that at least 32 people have died and more than 700 others have been injured in the disaster.
A state of emergency has been declared as search and rescue teams work to find survivors trapped beneath the rubble of collapsed structures.
The United States has mobilized a disaster assistance team and task force to coordinate critical aid, including search and rescue teams and medical supplies.
US Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau described the earthquakes as 'devastating' and confirmed that the US is in touch with Venezuelan authorities.
The disaster comes amid warming ties between the US and the interim Venezuelan government led by Delcy Rodriguez after the seizure of former President Nicolas Maduro in January.
caption:
32 dead and 700 injured. Twin earthquakes have left Venezuela in ruins.

Two strong earthquakes struck west of Venezuela's capital, Caracas, on Wednesday afternoon, causing widespread destruction and toppling buildings across the country.

The interim president reported that at least 32 people have died and more than 700 others have been injured in the disaster.

A state of emergency has been declared as search and rescue teams work to find survivors trapped beneath the rubble of collapsed structures.

The United States has mobilized a disaster assistance team and task force to coordinate critical aid, including search and rescue teams and medical supplies.

US Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau described the earthquakes as 'devastating' and confirmed that the US is in touch with Venezuelan authorities.

The disaster comes amid warming ties between the US and the interim Venezuelan government led by Delcy Rodriguez after the seizure of former President Nicolas Maduro in January.
